plain: A petty objection about a small point

webster.text: A start or turn from the point in question, or from plain truth; an evasion; a cavil; a pretense; as, to answer a sound argument by quibbles.

more.text: To evade the point in question, or plain truth, by artifice, play upon words, caviling or any conceit; to trifle in argument or discourse.

example.quote: It is well that these objections were not made by a lawyer : they would have been called quibbles, and he would have been accused of having learned them at the bar.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, Massachusetts Convention, Mr. AMES, February 5, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
